primary_headline: Bitcoin risks extended retreat as April rally was futures-driven: CryptoQuant
combined_key_facts: CryptoQuant warns that the recent Bitcoin price rally in April was primarily driven by the futures market, not an increase in spot demand.
A decline in the 'spot-to-futures volume ratio' suggests the rally was speculative and may not be sustainable.
Historically, similar patterns where futures trading dominates have preceded extended price declines for Bitcoin.
The market is showing signs of being 'overheated' with a high ratio of speculators compared to long-term holders.
Decrypt highlights that the surge was built on 'shaky ground', echoing the sentiment that the rally lacks fundamental support.

# Bitcoin risks extended retreat as April rally was futures-driven: CryptoQuant

[Latest News](https://cointelegraph.com/category/latest-news)Published May 1, 2026

Futures drove up Bitcoin's price in April while spot demand declined, which CryptoQuant warned has historically preceded extended price declines.

![Image 10](https://payload.cointelegraph.com/api/article-covers/file/HI%20marketsPro%20one-stop%20institutional-grade%20crypto%20intelligence%20dashboard%20Bitcoin.jpg?prefix=media%2Farticle-covers)

Bitcoin could be setting up for a multimonth price decline, after a rally in April driven mainly by futures traders while spot demand declined, according to the crypto analytics firm CryptoQuant.

Bitcoin gained around 20% in April, rising from $66,000 to a peak of $79,000 in a rally “driven entirely by growth in perpetual futures demand,” CryptoQuant said in a [report](https://cryptoquant.com/insights/research/69f3805fe2872616b411be88-30-April-2026-Speculative-Rally-Bitcoins-April-Price-Surge-Was-Fueled-by-Perpetu) on Thursday.

Meanwhile, spot demand for Bitcoin contracted throughout the rally, “indicating that the market’s marginal buyer was speculative, not fundamental,” it said.

“The divergence between rising price and contracting spot demand is one of the clearest on-chain signals that price gains are speculative rather than structural,” CryptoQuant added.
